title: In vitro Cell Culture Model for Toxic Inhaled Chemical Testing
protocol: Obtain rat cardiomyocytes from male rats (240-260 g) using previously described methods.
Anesthetize animals with an intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital (100 mg/kg).
Remove hearts into 10.0 ml, 1 mM Ca2+ containing Krebs Ringer buffer, pH 7.4.
Rinse the hearts 5-6 times to remove blood.
Switch to a Ca2+ free Krebs Ringer buffer containing 0.02% protease and 0.06% collagenase A (5.0 ml/heart).
Incubate the hearts in this solution for 10-15 min at 37 °C with occasional shaking.
Wash out the enzymatic solution with Ca2+ free Krebs Ringer buffer for an additional 5 min.
Release cells from flaccid tissue using a 25 ml pipette by pipetting the suspension up and down several times.
Separate the cells from tissue by filtering through a 70 μm nylon mesh.
Allow the cells to settle in Krebs Ringer buffer containing 0.1 mM Ca2+.
Suspend the cell pellet in 1.0 ml Krebs Ringer buffer containing 0.2 mM Ca2+.
Carefully layer 5.0 ml of 60 μg/ml bovine serum albumin in 15 ml centrifuge tubes.
Allow cardiomyocytes to settle for 30 min.
Remove the supernatant cells and media carefully.
Repeat the layering step once more to further purify the cells.
Wash ventricular myocytes/cardiomyocytes gradually using buffers containing 0.25 mM, 0.5 mM, 0.75 mM, and 1.0 mM Ca2+.
Resuspend the cardiomyocytes in ACCT medium consisting of DMEM with specific additives.
Plate the cardiomyocytes at a density of 100 to 150 cells/mm² on laminin-coated culture dishes or glass coverslips.
Incubate the plates for 1 hr.
Wash the dishes with 2.0 ml ACCT medium after 1 hour.
Add 10.0 ml fresh media and incubate the cells further.
Procure human tracheobronchial tissues from National Disease Research Interchange under Institutional Review Board approved protocols.
Remove all connective tissue and lymph nodes from the tissue.
Make small pieces (~¼ inch) of the tissue.
Wash tissue several times in Lactated Ringer solution.
Add tissues to a 50 ml conical tube with protease solution (1% Protease/0.01% DNase in minimal essential media, MEM, tissue to fluid ratio (1:10)).
Rock the tissue at 4 °C overnight.
End the dissociation of the tissue by adding 10% fetal bovine serum.
Scrape the epithelial surface with a surgical scalpel.
Collect cells by centrifugation (2,000 rpm for 10 min).
Plate cells at passage one on collagen-coated snapwells in special ALI medium prepared as described by Fulcher et al.
Culture for 5 days before changing to air-liquid interface (ALI) by removing apical media.
Feed the cells using ALI media every alternate day and allow the cells to differentiate for additional 2-3 weeks (observe numerous beating cilia and mucus secretion).
Wash the apical surface with warm PBS along with media changes.
Contain the chlorine exposure system inside a qualified chemical hood with an operational face velocity of 100 fpm.
Operate the system under slight positive pressure (0.5 inches of water).
Feed dry air at 15 L/min into the system.
Regulate the Cl2 concentration using a compressed gas cylinder containing 1.0% Cl2 in dry nitrogen.
Use a Mass Flow Controller to deliver the Cl2 mixture through the system.
Regulate dilution airflow using a custom designed control panel.
Monitor and record chlorine concentrations using a data logger connected to a chlorine analyzer.
Measure flow rates within the chambers prior to exposure using a flow meter.
Remove the supernatant media from the cell cultures.
Add fresh basolateral media for airway epithelial cells in ALI cultures.
Pretreat cells with agents if required at this stage.
Expose ALI cultures of airway epithelial cells to Cl2 gas (50, 100, or 300 ppm) for 30 min.
Expose cardiomyocytes to Cl2 (50 or 100 ppm) for 15 min in sealed chambers.
Flush the exposure chambers with air until Cl2 level falls below 1 ppm.
Remove cells from the chambers once safe to open and handle.
Equilibrate chopstick electrodes in ALI media for 15 minutes before TER measurement.
Add warm media (1.0 ml) to the apical surface of the culture.
Add warm media (2.0 ml) to the basolateral surface of the culture.
Measure the electrical resistance across the cell layer using chopstick electrodes.
Subtract the resistance measured across a cell-free culture support from the total resistance to yield TER.
Add fresh ALI media (2.0 ml) to the basolateral surface post exposure.
Incubate the cell at room temperature.
Collect supernatant media at 4 and 24 hours.
Measure caspase 3/7 activity in the media supernatants using a commercial caspase 3/7 assay kit.
Suspend the protein lysate (20 μg) in 5x reduced sample buffer and boil for 5 minutes.
Subject the protein lysate to SDS-PAGE (4-15%).
Transfer the separated proteins to a nitrocellulose membrane by electrophoretic blotting.
Incubate the membrane with 5% milk in wash buffer (PBS + 0.1% detergent) to block non-specific binding.
Probe the membranes with primary antibodies against SERCA2 or sarcomeric actin at a 1:1,000 dilution overnight at 4 °C.
Wash and incubate membranes with the respective peroxidase-conjugated secondary antibodies.
Develop for detection using a commercial peroxidase detection kit as described before.
Treat live cells grown on inserts or glass coverslips in 6-well plates with 0.4% Triton-X-100 in 10 mM sodium citrate buffer for 20 minutes after rinsing with PBS.
Block nonspecific binding by treating the cells with 5% donkey serum for 20 minutes.
Incubate the cells with non-specific IgG or individual primary antibodies specific to sarcomeric actin or Ki-67.
Wash the cells with PBS.
Incubate with fluorescent-conjugated secondary antibodies to detect the primary antibody.
Add a nuclear stain (1 μg/ml DAPI).
Wash the cells with PBS.
Mount coverslips using commercial mounting media.
Visualize the staining using a fluorescent microscope.
